_about: Chef GRDN's 8 existing recipes, exported 2026-11-08 from the Claude artifact. ingredients_text and steps_text use the artifact's line format: one item/step per line, a line starting with '## ' starts a section. scripts/seed.ts must parse ingredients_text with src/lib/quantity.ts into the recipes.ingredients JSON shape, split steps_text into [{section, steps}], and upsert by slug.

recipes.title: Crispy Miso-Glazed Salmon with Chili Miso Broth
recipes.ingredients_text:
## Salmon
4 salmon fillets (6–7 oz each), skin on
Kosher salt
Neutral oil (avocado or grapeseed)
## Miso glaze
3 tbsp white miso paste
1 tbsp mirin (no mirin: 1 tsp honey + 1 tsp rice vinegar)
1 tsp soy sauce
1–2 tbsp water, to loosen
## Chili miso broth
4 cups dashi or light chicken broth
2 tbsp white miso
1 tsp soy sauce
1 tsp rice vinegar
1 red chili, thinly sliced (divided)
## Garnish / veg
1 large bunch enoki mushrooms, trimmed
2 scallions, thinly sliced
Microgreens (optional)
recipes.steps_text:
## Make the glaze
In a small saucepan combine the white miso, mirin (or honey + rice vinegar), soy sauce and 1–2 tbsp water.
Simmer gently for 2–3 minutes until smooth and slightly thickened. Remove from heat and let cool.
## Prep the salmon
Pat salmon completely dry. Lightly salt both sides, especially the skin.
Let sit at room temperature for 10–15 minutes.
Right before cooking, brush glaze onto the flesh side only. Do not glaze the skin.
## Cook the salmon (crispy skin)
Heat a stainless steel or cast iron pan over medium and add a thin layer of neutral oil.
When the oil shimmers, place salmon skin side down. Press gently with a spatula for 10–15 seconds to prevent curling.
Cook 4–5 minutes without moving, until the skin is crispy and most of the cooking is done from the bottom.
Flip and cook 1–2 more minutes. Remove and rest.
## Make the chili miso broth
Warm broth in a pot (do not boil). Add half the sliced chili and let steep 5–10 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk the miso with a ladle of warm broth until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.
Add soy sauce and rice vinegar. Keep warm on low (do not boil).
## Cook the enoki
Heat a small amount of oil in a pan over medium. Sauté the enoki for 1–2 minutes and lightly salt.
## To plate
Ladle a small pool of broth into a shallow bowl.
Place salmon on top, skin side up, and add the enoki.
Garnish with fresh chili slices, scallions and microgreens.

recipes.title: Duck Miso Carbonara
recipes.ingredients_text:
## Pasta
8.8 oz fresh pasta (or ~10 oz dried spaghetti)
## Protein
1 duck breast
2–3 slices thick-cut bacon (optional but recommended)
Salt
Black pepper
## Sauce
2 whole eggs
2 egg yolks
½ cup finely grated parmesan
1 tbsp white miso paste
Fresh cracked black pepper
1 tbsp butter (optional, for extra richness)
## Aromatics / finish
1 clove garlic, minced
Fresh parsley, finely chopped
Micro arugula (optional but great)
Small pinch MSG (optional)
recipes.steps_text:
## Render the duck
Score the duck skin in a crosshatch pattern (don’t cut into the meat). Season both sides with salt.
Place duck skin side down in a cold pan and turn the heat to medium-low.
Render slowly for 6–8 minutes, until the skin is deeply golden and the fat has rendered out.
Flip and cook 2–4 minutes more (medium-rare preferred).
Remove and rest at least 5 minutes. Slice thinly before serving.
## Cook the bacon
In the same pan with the duck fat, cook the bacon until crispy. Remove and roughly chop.
Leave about 2 tbsp of fat in the pan.
## Cook the pasta
Boil heavily salted water and cook the pasta until just al dente.
Reserve ½ cup pasta water before draining.
## Make the sauce
In a bowl whisk the eggs, yolks, parmesan, white miso, generous black pepper and a pinch of MSG (optional) until smooth.
## Build the carbonara
Lower the heat on the duck fat pan. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds; do not brown.
Add the drained pasta directly to the pan and toss to coat in the fat.
Remove the pan from the heat. Slowly pour in the egg mixture while tossing constantly.
Add splashes of reserved pasta water until the sauce is glossy and silky. The heat from the pasta should emulsify the sauce, not scramble it.
## Finish
Fold in the crispy bacon.
Plate and top with sliced duck, parsley, micro arugula, extra parmesan and fresh cracked pepper.
notes: The miso adds umami depth but shouldn’t taste “Asian.” It should just taste richer.
Keep heat low when adding eggs to avoid scrambling.
Duck fat makes this extremely luxurious. No cream needed.

recipes.title: Gordon's Ground Turkey Chili
recipes.intro: A big 2 lb batch, first made around October 2025.
recipes.ingredients_text:
2 lb ground turkey
1 onion, diced
~1 pint diced carrots
4–5 cloves garlic, minced
28 oz kidney beans, drained and rinsed
14 oz black beans, drained and rinsed
14 oz corn, drained
56 oz canned tomatoes
6–8 cups chicken broth or water
Tomato paste
## Spices
2–3 tbsp chili powder
1–1½ tbsp cumin
2 tsp–1 tbsp smoked paprika
1½ tsp oregano
1 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp onion powder
~1½ tsp salt, then adjust
½ tsp black pepper
¼–½ tsp cayenne (optional)
A small pinch of cinnamon, cocoa powder or sugar for depth (optional)
recipes.steps_text:
Brown the turkey for about 8–10 minutes, breaking it up. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and carrots for 6–8 minutes.
Add the garlic for about 30 seconds, then add some tomato paste.
Add the spices and let them bloom briefly in the oil.
Add the tomatoes, beans, corn, and broth or water. Simmer about 15 minutes.
Give it 3–5 quick pulses with an immersion blender. Just enough to thicken the base while keeping plenty of chunks.
Add the turkey back and simmer uncovered for another 20–25 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for 10–15 minutes before eating.
notes: The immersion-blender step is the unusual part. It makes the chili much thicker and creamier without adding flour or anything else.

recipes.title: Miso Brothy Chicken Bowls
recipes.ingredients_text:
## Chicken marinade (30 minutes)
4 chicken thighs
2 tbsp white miso
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp rice vinegar
2 tsp honey
1 tsp sesame oil
2 garlic cloves, minced
## Broth
16 oz chicken stock (the original uses Kettle & Fire mushroom chicken)
4 garlic cloves, minced
¼ inch ginger, sliced into chunks
2 tbsp lemon juice
2 tbsp orange juice
1 tbsp miso paste
1 tbsp soy sauce
2 tsp fish sauce
A little neutral cooking oil
## Herb salad
1 green onion, chopped
Parsley and cilantro, chopped
Juice of ½ lemon
1 tsp sesame oil
## To serve
Rice
Chili oil
recipes.steps_text:
Mix the marinade ingredients, add the chicken thighs and marinate for 30 minutes.
Sear the chicken in a cast iron pan until cooked through. Slice.
For the broth, heat a little neutral oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add the rest of the broth ingredients and cook until the miso has dissolved.
Mix the herb salad ingredients together.
Put the chicken over rice, pour the broth over it, top with the herb salad and serve with chili oil.

recipes.title: Gordon's One-Pot Skillet Rice
recipes.ingredients_text:
1 lb ground turkey or chicken
5–6 cloves garlic, crushed
2 cups long-grain white rice
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, with their juice
½ bag (about 6 oz) frozen mixed veggies
4 cups chicken broth
1–1½ cups shredded cheese (cheddar, Monterey Jack or a Mexican blend)
Chopped parsley or cilantro, to finish
Flaky salt, to finish
## Spices
1 tbsp Italian seasoning
1 tsp cumin
1 tsp chili powder
1 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp salt (½ tsp if your broth isn't low-sodium)
½ tsp black pepper
½ tsp MSG
recipes.steps_text:
In a large, deep skillet with a lid, brown the turkey over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the rice and stir for 2–3 minutes to toast it.
Add all the spices and stir for about 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, then the frozen veggies and the broth. Stir, scrape up anything stuck to the bottom and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 25 minutes.
Scatter the cheese over the top, cover again and let it steam for 1–2 minutes until melted.
Finish with chopped parsley or cilantro and a pinch of flaky salt.
notes: Spice amounts are a starting point. Adjust to taste.
Go easy on the salt if the broth isn't low-sodium. The MSG adds salt too.
Don't lift the lid during the 25 minutes. The rice needs the steam.

recipes.title: Miso Corn Soup
recipes.ingredients_text:
4 corn cobs
8 cups water
2 chicken bouillon cubes
Scallion whites
~2 tsp grated ginger (to taste)
1–2 tbsp miso paste
recipes.steps_text:
Combine corn cobs, water, bouillon cubes, scallion whites and ginger. Bring to a boil, then simmer to pull flavor from the cobs.
Remove and discard the scallion whites.
Immersion-blend the pot until smooth.
Strain out the solids for a smooth soup.
Off the heat (so it doesn't turn bitter), stir in 1–2 tbsp miso paste to taste.

recipes.title: Kimchi Gazpacho
recipes.ingredients_text:
Carrots
Onion
Kimchi
Garlic
Ginger
Kimchi juice
Chicken stock
Apples
Heavy cream
Sesame oil
Sugar
Rice vinegar (to finish)
recipes.steps_text:
Blend carrots, onion, kimchi, garlic and ginger with kimchi juice and chicken stock until smooth.
Add apples, heavy cream and a splash of sesame oil; blend again.
Season with sugar to balance.
Finish with rice vinegar stirred in at the end. Chill before serving.

recipes.title: Lasagna Soup
recipes.intro: All the flavor of lasagna in a pot. 10 min prep, 40 min cook.
recipes.source_label: Lauren Allen, Tastes Better From Scratch
recipes.ingredients_text:
## Soup
½ lb lean ground beef
½ lb ground Italian sausage
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 yellow onion, chopped
1 tbsp olive oil
3 cloves garlic, minced
2 tbsp tomato paste
24 oz marinara sauce (or 1 batch homemade)
¼ tsp red pepper flakes
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 2 tsp dried)
½ tsp dried oregano
1 tsp dried basil
7 cups low-sodium chicken broth (or vegetable broth)
9 lasagna noodles, broken into pieces
2 cups fresh spinach leaves (optional)
## Cheese topping
10 oz ricotta (or cottage cheese)
1 cup shredded mozzarella
½ cup freshly grated parmesan
Fresh basil, for serving
recipes.steps_text:
## Soup
In a large pot over medium-high heat, brown the ground beef and sausage, seasoning with salt and pepper as it cooks. Drain the grease and set the meat aside.
In the same pot, heat the olive oil over medium. Sauté the onion for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, then add the garlic for another 1–2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, marinara, spices and broth. Return the meat to the pot.
Bring to a boil, add the lasagna noodles (broken into quarters), then lower to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are tender.
Stir in the spinach, if using.
## Serve
In a small bowl, mix the mozzarella, parmesan and ricotta.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top each with a scoop of the cheese mixture and garnish with fresh basil.
notes: Leftovers keep 3–4 days in the fridge.
Make ahead: cook through adding the meat and broth, refrigerate, then add the noodles and cheese when serving.
Freezes for 2–3 months without the cheese. Thaw overnight and reheat gently on the stove.
Any pasta shape works in place of the lasagna noodles.
The original post also has slow cooker and vegetarian versions.
